correctness.rationale: For real alpha,b>0 and t>=0, direct diagonalization of [[-b,t],[t,b t^alpha]] yields F=b+u for t<=1 with u[b(1+t^alpha)+u]=t^2, and the positive eigenvalue branch increases for t>=1. Implicit differentiation fixes the sign reversal at b^2=4/(alpha t^(alpha-2)((alpha-2)t^alpha-2)); the threshold is decreasing in t and terminates at alpha>4, b_c=2/sqrt(alpha(alpha-4)). The exact F(t)>F(1) comparison confines all positive backward overshoot to b>=const epsilon^(-1/2), 1-t=O(epsilon). The uniform square-root expansion there yields L(beta,s)=s(beta^2-1)/(4 beta^3)-s^2/beta. Its unique global maximum is 1/(100sqrt5) at beta=sqrt5,s=1/10; compactness and the vanishing beta->infinity envelope establish global limit and every maximizing-pair scale. Exact symbolic checks independently confirmed stationary and expansion identities; finite checker samples do not prove universality.
